title: Prebuilt Search Engines
readerIntent: Select and qualify an available Nodics search implementation.
summary: The generic search module is the caller contract; Elasticsearch is the current engine-specific adapter.

sections.heading: Provider-neutral search
items: Owns secured schema and index routes.
Owns normalized models, pipelines, errors, cache policy, and fallback rules.
Must remain free of engine client calls and customer index topology.

sections.heading: Elasticsearch adapter
items: Owns connection handling, raw Elastic search-model loading, operation mapping, and client calls.
Supports health, refresh, exists, get, search, save, bulk, update, remove, remove by query, schema, and index lifecycle operations.
Normalizes the historical hosts configuration to the client nodes option.
Is guarded: deterministic tests exist, but each production deployment requires live cluster, security, version, recovery, and performance qualification.

sections.heading: Configuration boundary
paragraphs: Endpoints, credentials, index names, aliases, tenant routing, timeouts, retries, refresh, mappings, and engine topology belong to layered configuration or approved secret/runtime governance—not provider-neutral business source.

sections.heading: Elasticsearch maturity
paragraphs: The adapter provides implemented mapping for the normalized operations, but production approval is specific to the selected Elasticsearch and client versions, security configuration, topology, mappings, and workload.
A local single-node instance with security disabled is suitable only for local integration testing and must never define committed production defaults.

sections.heading: Capability comparison
items: Confirm every required normalized operation.
Confirm mapping, analyzer, aggregation, pagination, bulk, alias, and refresh semantics.
Confirm partial bulk failure and conflict behavior.
Confirm tenant routing and permission filters cannot be bypassed.
Confirm retry and timeout behavior is safe.
Record unsupported engine features explicitly.

sections.heading: Adding another engine
paragraphs: OpenSearch, Solr, or another engine requires its own provider module implementing the same normalized boundary. The adapter owns vendor translation; business models and generic search services remain unchanged.
Completion requires live provider tests, supported-version documentation, security, performance, failure, migration, backup, and recovery evidence.

sections.heading: Production evidence
items: Authenticated encrypted connection and secret rotation.
Representative query and indexing load.
Cluster, shard, replica, and capacity behavior.
Node loss, partition, reconnect, and partial bulk failure.
Snapshot restore, reindex, alias rollback, and upgrade.
Dashboards, alerts, runbooks, and known limitations.

sections.heading: Selection reminder
items: Choose an engine only after matching query, scale, consistency, tenancy, operations, cost, recovery, and supported-version needs.
A locally installed Elasticsearch instance proves development integration, not production security, clustering, backup, upgrade, or capacity.
Keep selection configurable and qualify every enabled provider against the same normalized nSearch contract.
